newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DELIGHTED MALDINI PRAISES HIS PLAYERS AFTER VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DELIGHTED MALDINI PRAISES HIS PLAYERS AFTER VICTORY.

text.p: Elated Italian coach Cesare Maldini praised his players for the discipline and commitment they showed in their 1-0 win over England in their crucial World Cup group two qualifier on Wednesday.
Maldini, who has happy memories of Wembley after being a member of the Milan team which won the European Cup at the stadium in 1963, thoroughly enjoyed his return visit.
"It was a great game, we played as we planned and got a great result against a great team. My deepest compliments to my players, they were very good.
"I had very little to do with it, I just have to thank the players."
Maldini, who succeeded the unpopular Arrigo Sacchi as Italian coach last month, also played down the adulation surrounding Gianfranco Zola's 19th-minute winner.
"Zola is a very imporatant player for us but so are the other 10. Zola scored the goal but that is his job."
He also played down the impact the victory could have on Italy's chances of automatically qualifying for the finals next year as group winners.
"We just want to appreciate and enjoy this success," he said. "We'll start thinking about the next game and what it means in two weeks time."
England coach Glenn Hoddle, who saw his side lose for the first time since he succeeded Terry Venables as coach after Euro 96, was philosophical afterwards.
"It was a setback but not a disaster. There's a lot of football still to be played in this group and they still have difficult matches to play in Georgia and Poland.
"Now we've got to bounce back. We are very very disappointed. They had one chance and they scored it and the game went their way.
"We always knew it was going to be a very tight game. We couldn't have attacked more than we did in the second half and if little things had gone our way it would have been a different story.
"They played five at the back with man-to-man marking and made it difficult to get behind them. We just couldn't open them up."
Hoddle also revealed he had to make late changes to his planned team because of injuries to goalkeeper David Seaman, defender Tony Adams and midfielder Paul Gascoigne.
"Seaman pulled out this morning and in a way the team was forced upon us. We could have done without that but I don't want to use that as an excuse."
